physics: em.modes2d vector, lossless SOI strip and 400 x 400 nm square core: n_eff and TE fraction
role: code-to-code comparison of n_eff and the TE fraction; not analytical acceptance or convergence evidence

settings.function: scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs on EMpy.modesolvers.FD.VFDModeSolver.build_matrix(), fields by VFDModeSolver.compute_other_fields and FDMode.normalize, in place of VFDModeSolver.solve()
settings.why: solve() fixes which=LR with shift-invert, which asks for the eigenvalues just above the shift and did not converge at 20 nm; LM with the shift at the core index gives the highest modes
settings.kept: the two largest guided n_eff of 4, confirmed at the coarsest grid by a second solve with 6 eigenvalues
settings.grid: nodes on the window and core edges, each segment in equal cells of at most h

inputs.te_fraction: sum A |E_x|^2 divided by sum A (|E_x|^2 + |E_y|^2) over every cell of the window, A the cell area, E at cell centres
inputs.grid: nodes on every window and core edge; each segment in equal cells of at most the step h
inputs.te_fraction_band: te_fraction_<case>_d20 and _d40: the same fraction over the cells whose centre lies at a distance of at least 20 or 40 nm from the core rectangle's boundary, inside or outside (inside: the smallest distance to its four edges; outside: the Euclidean distance to the rectangle)

matched: PEC on all walls (VFDModeSolver boundary SSAA)
material indices: physmat Si and SiO2 at 1550 nm, as plain numbers
the TE fraction definition, weighted by cell area
not_matched: discretization: finite differences on a near-uniform rectilinear grid against edge finite elements on a graded mesh
interfaces: staircase cell-centred permittivity against mesh-conforming interfaces
samples: cell centres against triangle centroids
